title: Running a feature as seven roles, each in its own thread
summary: I split a UI feature across parallel agent threads, one per role. Work passes by pull request and written spec, not by chat, and the reviewer is never the author.

stat.label: roles, each owning named files or a repository

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: One agent thread doing design, components, screens, an API and a deploy gets slow and loses context. It also reviews its own work, which is the weakest review there is.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: A skill defines seven roles: designer, kit, frontend, backend, DevOps, QA and accessibility, and reviewer. Each role owns files or a repository and has its own skill.

Work moves in a fixed order: spec, contract, components, integration, deploy, then review and QA. A role hands over by pull request and by the written spec. A thread messages a peer only when the coordinator says so. The reviewer is never the author of the pull request. Infrastructure pull requests merge through the same open-PR gate as everything else.

table.caption: The roles and what each owns
rows: The spec the other roles build from
Proof that the feature works and is accessible
An independent review of each pull request

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: The lab dashboard was the pilot. The kit and DevOps roles ran in separate threads. One thread played backend and frontend together.

sections.heading: Lesson
paragraphs: Agents work best like a small team: clear ownership, written handoffs and a reviewer with no stake in the code.
